{"predictors": [
  {"name": "Age of the firm", 
   "construction": "Calculate the number of years since the firm's initial public offering (IPO).", 
   "rationale": "Older firms may be more stable and less risky, leading to potentially higher returns.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Older firms"},

  {"name": "Productivity Growth", 
   "construction": "Calculate the year-over-year percentage change in revenue per employee.", 
   "rationale": "Firms with growing productivity may be more efficient and competitive, leading to potentially higher returns.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with high productivity growth"},

  {"name": "Revenue Concentration", 
   "construction": "Calculate revenue concentration as the percentage of total revenue derived from a single customer or client.", 
   "rationale": "A high concentration could indicate customer captivity but also customer concentration risk.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with low revenue concentration"},

  {"name": "R&D Intensity", 
   "construction": "Calculate R&D expense divided by total revenues.", 
   "rationale": "Firms with high R&D intensity may be more innovative and have greater growth opportunities.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with high R&D intensity"},

  {"name": "Operating Leverage", 
   "construction": "Calculate the ratio of fixed costs to variable costs.", 
   "rationale": "Firms with high operating leverage may have higher profit margins in good times, but higher risk in bad times.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with low operating leverage"},

  {"name": "Management Ownership", 
   "construction": "Calculate the percentage of shares owned by management.", 
   "rationale": "Firms where management has significant ownership may be better aligned with shareholder interests.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms where management has high ownership"},

  {"name": "Employee Satisfaction", 
   "construction": "Use surveys or other public data to calculate a measure of employee satisfaction.", 
   "rationale": "Firms with happier employees may have lower turnover and higher productivity, leading to higher returns.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with high employee satisfaction"},

  {"name": "Product Market Competition", 
   "construction": "Calculate the firm's market share in its primary industry.", 
   "rationale": "Firms facing less competition may have higher pricing power, potentially leading to higher returns.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with higher market share"},

  {"name": "Customer Loyalty", 
   "construction": "Use surveys or other public data to calculate a measure of customer loyalty.", 
   "rationale": "Firms with loyal customers may have more predictable revenue streams and potentially higher returns.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with high customer loyalty"},

  {"name": "Pension Fund Status", 
   "construction": "Calculate the funded status of the company's pension plan (pension assets - pension obligations).", 
   "rationale": "Underfunded pension obligations may pose financial risk.", 
   "higher_returns_for": "Firms with more fully funded pensions"}
]}
